question: Akshat invested ₹90,625 at 8% p.a. for 1 year at compound interest, compounded half yearly. The amount received by him is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **half-yearly compounding**, the **Rate** becomes 8% ÷ 2 = 4% and the **Time** becomes 1 × 2 = 2 periods.

Using the **Ratio Method** for 4% (which is 1/25):

Initial : Final = 25 : 26

For 2 periods: 25² : 26² → 625 : 676

625 units = ₹90,625 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹145

676 units = 676 × 145 = ₹98,020

**∴ The correct answer is ₹98,020.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹90,625

**Rate (R)** = 8% p.a.

**Time (T)** = 1 year

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ

Where r = Rate per compounding period, n = Number of periods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/916696dd9ba159aa7e7ffe6e341ee822ad770ca188f11a8c288106200b78f60d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Effective Rate for half-yearly = 8% ÷ 2 = 4%

⇒ Number of half-yearly periods in 1 year = 1 × 2 = 2

⇒ A = 90625 × (1 + 4/100)²

⇒ A = 90625 × (104/100) × (104/100)

⇒ A = 90625 × (26/25) × (26/25)

⇒ A = (90625 ÷ 625) × 676

⇒ A = 145 × 676

⇒ A = ₹98,020

**∴ The correct answer is ₹98,020.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compounding Half-Yearly Rule

When interest is compounded **half-yearly**, the annual rate is divided by 2 and the time period is multiplied by 2.

Effective Rate of Interest

The effective rate for two successive periods of r% is given by [r + r + (r × r)/100]%. For 4%, it is 4 + 4 + 0.16 = 8.16%.

Compound Interest Formula

CI = Amount − Principal = P[(1 + R/100)ⁿ − 1].
